holidays.name: Mario Day (MAR10 Day)
holidays.description: Video game fans celebrate Nintendo's mustachioed plumber by playing Mario games, wearing red caps, and eating mushroom-themed snacks. The date is a pun because 'MAR10' looks like 'MARIO' when written out.
holidays.origin: The holiday grew out of the date's visual pun and became an unofficial fan celebration. Nintendo has embraced it over the years with sales, announcements, and special events.
holidays.funFact: Mario first appeared in 1981 as 'Jumpman' in Donkey Kong, where he was a carpenter rather than a plumber.

holidays.name: National Blueberry Popover Day
holidays.description: A day dedicated to the light, airy, hollow pastry that puffs up in the oven and gets stuffed with juicy blueberries. People celebrate by baking popovers, slathering them with butter or jam, and enjoying them at brunch.
holidays.origin: Popovers are a variation of Yorkshire pudding and have been popular in America since the 1800s. Food calendar makers designated this day to honor the blueberry-filled version.
holidays.funFact: Popovers get their name because the batter expands so much in the oven that it 'pops over' the top of the baking tin.

holidays.name: International Day of Awesomeness
holidays.description: A day to embrace your inner awesomeness and do something fun, bold, or generous. People are encouraged to celebrate their own accomplishments and compliment others on theirs.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial, internet-era observance that spread through social media and holiday calendars. It has no single known founder, which fits its casual spirit.
holidays.funFact: The word 'awesome' originally meant 'inspiring awe or dread' and was used in religious contexts before becoming slang for 'really cool' in the 20th century.

holidays.name: Salvation Army Day
holidays.description: This observance honors the charitable organization known for its red kettles, thrift stores, and disaster relief. People celebrate by volunteering, donating, or learning about the group's work.
holidays.origin: The date commemorates the Salvation Army's arrival in the United States in 1880, when George Scott Railton and a small group of women began their work in New York City.
holidays.funFact: The Salvation Army started in London in 1865 as the 'Christian Mission' before being renamed in 1878 with a military-style structure, including ranks and uniforms.

holidays.name: Harriet Tubman Day
holidays.description: A day of remembrance honoring the legendary abolitionist who led enslaved people to freedom on the Underground Railroad. Schools and communities mark it with history lessons, readings, and tributes.
holidays.origin: Tubman died on March 10, 1913, in Auburn, New York. In 1990, the U.S. Congress designated March 10 as Harriet Tubman Day.
holidays.funFact: Tubman also served as a Union Army scout and spy, and she led the Combahee River Raid in 1863, which freed more than 700 people.
